Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book:
- The May 3, 2023 FOMC statement remains guarded-hawkish (moderate growth, robust jobs, elevated inflation, 25 bp hike to 5–5.25%, ongoing balance-sheet runoff) while noting tighter credit conditions will weigh on activity.
- SLOOS corroborates a credit-led drag: broad-based tightening across C&I, CRE, and consumer lending; weaker demand; and expectations of further tightening.
- Beige Book insights tilt the outlook more negative: only a few Districts indicated growth while many reported little or mixed change; consumer spending generally steady with auto sales steady; price growth described as moderate; and crucially, lending volumes and loan demand declined as rates rose. Regional detail (e.g., Boston and others) points to softer home sales and moderating wage growth, with manufacturing and retail mixed.
Implication: The Beige Book broadens and validates the SLOOS signal of a near-term credit and demand slowdown, increasing downside risks to growth and employment while gradually relieving inflation pressures. Net effect: sentiment shifts further negative from the SLOOS-adjusted view.
